description: We are a team from Romania trying to expand our knowledge.
summary:
Our team, Starcloud, through our project, RO-MARS, explores Romania’s potential as a terrestrial analog for future lunar and Martian missions. We developed a geographical visualization that identifies and characterizes Romanian environments sharing geological, topographical, and environmental features with the Moon and Mars.

Using open NASA and ESA datasets alongside scientific research, we investigated five key locations: Racoș, Berca, Salina Turda, Scărișoara Cave, and Huda lui Papară. We compared their terrain, mineral composition, geological structures, and environmental conditions with extraterrestrial volcanic plains, mud-volcanic formations, chloride-bearing deposits, ice-rich environments, and underground cavities.

Our project addresses the challenge by highlighting Romanian locations where exploration technologies, rover mobility, resource detection, and subsurface operations could potentially be studied and tested before future space missions.

By demonstrating Romania’s geological diversity and scientific potential, we aim to contribute to safer, more efficient space exploration while making planetary science more accessible. Our work connects terrestrial research with extraterrestrial exploration, showing that preparing for humanity’s future beyond Earth can begin much closer to home.
details:
We collected and analyzed open satellite data from NASA and ESA, alongside geological research and scientific publications. We investigated five Romanian locations and their respective planetary counterparts:

  • Racoș: Martian basaltic plains and lunar mare basalts.
  • Berca: Martian pitted cones and mounds.
  • Salina Turda: Martian chloride-bearing deposits.
  • Scărișoara Cave: Martian exposed subsurface ice and lunar permanently shadowed regions.
  • Huda lui Papară: Martian cave skylights and lunar pits.

For each location, we considered 14 characteristics: elevation, slope, surface roughness, terrain morphology, obstacle distribution, rock types, mineral composition, geological structures, sedimentary characteristics, temperature, humidity, precipitation, wind and airflow, and seasonal variation.

Our geographical visualization brings these characteristics together, allowing users to explore Romanian landscapes and understand their similarities and differences compared with extraterrestrial environments.

We used several open scientific datasets and platforms, including:

  • NASADEM for elevation and terrain characteristics.
  • ESA WorldCover for land-cover classification.
  • MOD11A1 for land surface temperatures.
  • LOLA, SLDEM2015 and LROC for lunar topography and surface morphology.
  • MOLA and HiRISE for Martian elevation and detailed terrain.
  • NASA Earthdata and the Planetary Data System for scientific data acquisition.
